anchor: A wet sheet and a flowing sea
note: A wet sheet: a sail kept wet so it holds the wind. Sailors used the phrase for fair sailing.
On the lee: on the sheltered side, away from the wind. Here England is left behind, downwind of the ship.

anchor: As his corpse to the rampart we hurried
note: Moore was fatally wounded at the battle of Corunna in January 1809. By his own wish he was buried before dawn in the ramparts of the town.

anchor: The sods with our bayonets turning
note: Sods: pieces of turf. The soldiers dig the grave quickly with their bayonets.
Reck: to care about, take heed of. He will pay little attention to what the enemy says.

anchor: That the foe was sullenly firing
note: The French under Soult followed the retreating British army across Spain to Corunna. The poem hears the enemy’s guns as the burial party finishes its work.
